name: Asturian

allophone_rules.notes: Unaccented ⟨i⟩ before a vowel is the first element of a rising diphthong or a triphthong, the semiconsonant [j] of pioyu, mieu (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) II.2 p. 24; Normes Ortográfiques (ALLA 2021) §1.6.1-§1.6.2 p. 26). An accented ⟨í⟩ is a hiatus (maíz, allegría) and keeps its full vowel (Normes Ortográfiques (ALLA 2021) §1.9.1.3 p. 45).

Unaccented ⟨u⟩ before a vowel is the semiconsonant [w] of fueya, güei (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) II.2 p. 24). An accented ⟨ú⟩ is a hiatus (falcatrúa, feúcu) (Normes Ortográfiques (ALLA 2021) §1.9.1.3 p. 45).

Unaccented ⟨i⟩ after a vowel closes a falling diphthong or a triphthong, the semivowel [i̯] of coméi, algaire (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) II.2 p. 24): allampiáis, estropiéis (Normes Ortográfiques (ALLA 2021) §1.6.2 p. 26).

Unaccented ⟨u⟩ after a vowel is the semivowel [u̯] of pautu, aniciáu (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) II.2 p. 24): Uviéu, mieu, fueu, llueu, faláu (Normes Ortográfiques (ALLA 2021) §1.6.2 p. 26; §1.9.1.2 p. 45).

/b/ (⟨b⟩ and ⟨v⟩ alike) is the fricative [β] between vowels, in br/bl after a vowel, and after any consonant except the nasal archiphoneme /N/; it is the stop [b] after a pause and after /N/ (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.5 p. 37): cebera, llavar, cabra, malvís, erbía.

/d/ is the fricative [ð] between vowels, in dr after a vowel, and after any consonant except /N/ and /L/; it is the stop [d] after a pause, after /N/ and after /L/ (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.6 pp. 37-38): rueda, cadril, surdir, desdexase; but candáu, lleldu.

/ɡ/ (⟨g⟩ and ⟨gu⟩) "realízase xeneralmente como velar fricativu sonoru": after /L/, /N/, /R/, /s/, /θ/ and /ʃ/, between vowels, and in gr/gl after a vowel (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.8 pp. 38-39): dalguién, llargu, fungar, esguedeyar, mugor, allegre, sieglu.
The same paragraph lists the start of a word after a pause among the fricative contexts of /ɡ/ (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.8 pp. 38-39).

/y/ is the affricate [ɟ͡ʝ] at the start of a word after a pause and after /N/, and the fricative [ʝ] between vowels and after other consonants (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.7 p. 38): yo; glayar, quemar yerba. Only the word-initial context is encoded. After /N/ inside a word (nenyures) the stress mark would split the affricate, so the fricative stays there.

After ⟨l⟩, ⟨n⟩ and ⟨s⟩ a single ⟨r⟩ "pronúnciase fuerte" (Normes Ortográfiques (ALLA 2021) §1.7.19.1 b p. 34; Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.19 p. 43): vienres, tienru, xenru, alredor, esriñonar, Israel.
The nasal archiphoneme /N/ is [m] before a bilabial (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.15 a p. 41): enmarcar, con mazanes.
/N/ is [ŋ] before a velar (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.15 g p. 41): concu, llongu, nun ganes.

/N/ is also [ŋ] "en final de pallabra ante vocal o ante final absolutu" (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.15 g p. 41): son hermanos, con orbayu, que xuban. A word transcribed alone stands before a pause.
/s/ at the end of a syllable or word is voiced before a voiced consonant (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.11 b-d p. 40): achisbar, fisgar, mesmu, rosnar, esllava, desdexase.
/θ/ at the end of a syllable or word is voiced before a voiced consonant (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.10 a p. 39): pazguatu, diz dos.
/ʃ/ at the end of a syllable or word is voiced before a voiced consonant (Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA 2001) III.1.12 b p. 40): pexdegatu, potax bono.

ancestors.notes: Primary descent from Hispanic Vulgar Latin, NW Iberian branch. Asturleonese diverged from Galaico-Portuguese roughly 9th–10th c. CE.

Gallaecian Celtic substrate: the Astures and neighbouring tribes of the Cantabrian coast shared cultural/linguistic affinities with the Gallaecian Celts. Castro culture influence; possible contribution to F-initial retention and prosodic patterns.
Suebi (Germanic) superstrate: the Kingdom of the Suebi (411–585 CE) controlled Gallaecia and extended into the Asturian-Cantabrian zone. ~200 lexical items and place-names.
Visigothic superstrate: pan-Iberian Germanic overlay after 585 CE. Less intense in the far north; Asturias was never fully under Visigothic control.
Andalusi Arabic: minimal direct contact given the north's brief or absent Moorish occupation. Some lexical borrowings through the Reconquista and repopulation movements.
Mozarabic adstrate: Romance of the Christian communities under Moorish rule in central and southern Iberia. Indirect contact through repopulation of the meseta.

notes: Standard Asturian, spoken in the Principality of Asturias (Spain), as the Academia de la Llingua Asturiana (ALLA) writes it. Spelling follows the Normes Ortográfiques (8th revised ed., 2021); the phonetic variants of the phonemes follow the Gramática de la Llingua Asturiana (3rd ed., 2001), to which Normes §1.1.7 (p. 14) sends the reader. Each allophone rule note gives its paragraph and page. VOWELS: 'Los fonemes vocálicos son: /a, e, i, o, u/' (Normes §1.2, p. 15). The open variants [ę] (repla, pex) and [ǫ] (xorra, voi) of Gramática II.2 (p. 24) have no stated context, so they stay in the allophone inventory and no rule produces them. ⟨i⟩ and ⟨u⟩ next to another vowel are the glides [j w] before the nucleus and [i̯ u̯] after it (Gramática II.2, p. 24); the diphthongs, the mixed diphthongs /iu, ui/ and the triphthongs are those of Normes §1.6.1-§1.6.2 (p. 26). ⟨y⟩ is the consonant /y/, but 'el fonema /i/ ye representáu cola lletra «y»' in the enclitic pronoun ⟨-y⟩ (dio-y pan, nun-y presta) and in the conjunction ⟨y⟩ (Normes §1.2.1.2, p. 15); word_exceptions carries both, and the pronoun's combinations -ylu, -yla, -ylo, -ylos, -yles (dá-yla, dán-ylo, Normes §1.9.1.4 c, p. 46). CONSONANTS: ⟨x⟩ /ʃ/, ⟨ll⟩ /ʎ/, ⟨ñ⟩ /ɲ/, ⟨ch⟩ /tʃ/, ⟨rr⟩ /r/ (Normes §1.7, pp. 27-34). ⟨h⟩ is mute (Normes §1.7.20, p. 34). In ⟨gue gui que qui⟩ the ⟨u⟩ 'nun representa nengún fonema' (Normes §1.2.2.2, p. 15); ⟨ü⟩ is pronounced (güei). A single ⟨r⟩ after ⟨l n s⟩ is strong and elsewhere inside the word weak (Normes §1.7.19.1, p. 34). WRITTEN DIALECT FEATURES: the 'ch vaqueira' ⟨ḷḷ⟩ or ⟨l.l⟩ is [t̺s̺, t's, ʈʂ, ʈ, ɖ] in the west, and 'nel restu del asturianu hay una [ʎ]' (Normes §1.1.3, p. 14), so this spec reads it as [ʎ] and ast-x-occident carries the western value. ⟨ts⟩ writes the western [ts] of /tʃ/ (cutsu, Normes §1.1.4, p. 14). ⟨yy⟩ writes the western [ky] of /y/ (muyyer, Normes §1.1.5, p. 14; 'soníu africáu palatal [kʸ]', Gramática I, p. 17); the spec writes it [kʲ]. ⟨ḥ⟩ and ⟨h.⟩ write the eastern aspiration (Normes §1.1.2, p. 13), '[h] o [x]' (Gramática I, p. 16); the spec writes [h]. ELISION: an apostrophe joins the elided word to the next, so l'agua, d'Uviéu and qu'entamar are each one phonological word; ⟨qu'⟩ before a vowel or ⟨h⟩ keeps the value /k/ (Gramática III.2.1, p. 43). HISTORY: Asturian continues Hispanic Vulgar Latin with Ĕ > /ie/, Ŏ > /ue/ and Latin F- kept (falar, filu) (Penny 2002). The Asturleonese family also includes Leonese, Mirandese, Rionorese and Guadramilese; the Leonese branch (ast-x-leon and its children) does not inherit the ALLA allophone rules, because the ALLA describes the speech of Asturias only.

stress.notes: Stress follows Normes Ortográfiques (ALLA 2021) §1.9.1, pp. 44-47. A written accent marks the stressed vowel. Without one, a word that ends in a vowel, ⟨-n⟩ or ⟨-s⟩ is paroxytone and a word that ends in another consonant is oxytone, because 'toles pallabres agudes acabaes en vocal, «-n» o «-s»' and 'toles pallabres llanes acabaes en consonante que nun seya nin «-n» nin «-s»' carry the accent (§1.9.1.1 a-b, p. 44): falen, mayu and vieyu are paroxytone; esconder and Enol are oxytone (Gramática V.2.2, p. 66). A final ⟨-l⟩ counts only after a vowel, so an enclitic ⟨'l⟩ (lleva'l) leaves the stress of its host where it was. A diphthong or a triphthong is one syllable (§1.6, p. 26) and takes the accent on its most open vowel (§1.9.1.2, p. 45: Uviéu, faláu, téunicu). An accent on the closed vowel marks a hiatus (§1.9.1.3, p. 45: maíz, feúcu, partíu, ruíu, influíu), and so does an accent on either vowel of /iu, ui/: cubriú is cu-bri-ú. CLITICS: cliticless_words lists the 'pallabres átones' of Gramática V.2.1.2 (p. 66): the articles, the relatives (que, quien, cuantu, cuando, onde, u ~ au, unaccented against the interrogatives, Normes §1.9.1.7 b, p. 47), the object pronouns with the enclitic ⟨-y⟩ and its combinations, the prepositions (ante, baxo, con, dende, pente, sobro) and the conjunctions (y, ya, o, nin, pero). The negation nun is a stressed adverb (Gramática V.2.1.1, p. 66).
